note: Recast from entry 90 of Roonwal & Chhotani (1997), the original in English. The alate is described from dealates in the original, hence no wing measurements. The diagnostic characters follow the keys to the alates and soldiers in that work (p. 571–572). The synonymy list, literature citations, figure numbers, type records, distribution and biology have been omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head length to the mandibular bases 2.6–2.7 mm, width 1.75–1.80 mm, mandibles rather short (mandible length/head length 0.65–0.69) and weakly curved forward, pronotum width/head width 0.81–0.88 and length/width 0.55–0.58; in the comparable fletcheri the mandibles are thicker, strongly incurved and relatively longer (that ratio about 0.72), the anterior margin of the pronotum broadly concave, the sides rather straight, width/head width about 0.95 and length/width 0.66. Alate head capsule pale yellowish brown, antenna 16 segments, the occipital suture visible only posteriorly with indistinct lateral arms, forewing scale length 1.3–1.5 and hindwing scale 0.73–0.85 mm; it differs from faveolus, in which the occipital suture is distinct and the wing scales shorter (forewing 1.0–1.13, hindwing 0.75–0.85 mm).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: (Dealate.) Head capsule, pronotum, wing scales and labrum pale yellowish brown; antennae, mesonotum and legs yellow to pale brown; abdomen chestnut brown. Head capsule moderate, the body densely covered with long hairs. Body length without wings 6.25–9.35 mm. Head capsule nearly rectangular, wider than long (length 1.33–1.60, width including eyes 1.68–1.80 mm); apart from the eyes the sides are nearly parallel in front of the posterior 1/3; posterior margin broadly rounded; occipital suture visible only on the posterior part of the head, lateral arms indistinct. Fontanelle indistinct. Antenna 16 segments; segment 1 the largest, segment 2 variable, about equal to segments 3 and 4 together or longer than segment 3, segments 3–5 ring-like, segment 4 the shortest. Eyes black, nearly circular (major diameter 0.45–0.50, minor diameter 0.40–0.45 mm). Ocelli colourless and transparent, small (major diameter 0.18–0.23, minor diameter 0.13–0.15 mm), about half their major diameter from the eye. Postclypeus nearly trapezoidal, hairy, indistinctly delimited from the frons and concolorous with it, anterior margin nearly straight; anteclypeus white, transparent, hairless. Mandibles as in the genus. Labrum dome-shaped, wider than long (width 0.50–0.58, length 0.45–0.50 mm), anterior margin nearly straight, hairy on the anterior part and on the surface. Pronotum nearly kidney-shaped, flat, densely covered with long and short hairs; narrower than the head width including the eyes, much wider than long (width 1.35–1.50, length 0.85–0.90 mm); anterior margin slightly concave, without a notch, anterolateral corners broadly rounded, the sides narrowing backwards to a rounded posterior margin. Legs long, densely hairy; femora swollen; tibiae slender, tibial spurs 3:2:2; tarsi 3-segmented. Abdomen densely hairy; cerci 2-segmented and hairy; abdominal styli absent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head brown, the rest paler. Head and thorax sparsely hairy, the abdomen densely hairy. Body length including the mandibles about 8.0–8.8 mm. Head slightly elongate, nearly rectangular (sides slightly convex), longer than wide (length 2.6–2.7, width 1.75–1.80 mm); occipital suture weak. Fontanelle minute, circular, slightly raised, situated in the anterior 1/3 of the head, the small fontanelle gland visible. Labrum dome-shaped, wider than long, the apical half with several long hairs (length 0.25–0.30, width 0.45 mm). Anteclypeus narrow; postclypeus large. Mandibles stout, shorter than the head (length 1.75–1.80 mm), thick at the base, the tip sharp and slightly incurved; the inner margin with a weak tooth in the basal 1/3 and a larger tooth slightly below it. Eyes degenerate, appearing as pale spots, no longer distinct in the type specimens examined; ocelli absent. Antenna 13–14 segments; segment 2 the smallest, segment 3 longer than segments 2 and 4. Postmentum long, rod-like, with a long narrow waist at the middle; the rod part bilobed (length 1.80–2.00, maximum width 0.70–0.75, waist width 0.25 mm). Pronotum flat, narrower than the head; length 0.80–0.90, width 1.45–1.55 mm; posterior margin rounded; anterior margin with a strong median concavity, posterior margin without one. Femora thick and swollen; apical tibial spurs 3:2:2; tarsi 3-segmented. Abdomen elongate; cerci short, about 0.15 mm long, 2-segmented; abdominal styli absent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Body yellow, hair weak; body length 4.7–6.1 mm. Head circular, slightly narrowing posteriorly (length 1.00–1.12, width 1.15–1.50 mm). Fontanelle minute. Eyes degenerate; ocelli absent. Labrum dome-shaped; length 0.38–0.50, width 0.40–0.45 mm. Anteclypeus large; postclypeus slightly inflated, the median longitudinal suture indistinct. Mandibles of the Stylotermes type. Pronotum much wider than long, narrower than the head (length 0.40–0.60, width 0.80–1.15 mm); anterior margin turned up and with a strong median concavity, posterior margin with a weak median concavity. Legs and abdomen as in the soldier.
